subproblem.title: Boundary mass transfer through a smooth cut-off (locality of d)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U₁ U₂ W V : Set (Eucl P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U₁ (m + 1)) (A : GeometricCurrentOn U₂ (m + 1)), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U₂ → IsCompact (closure V) → closure V ⊆ W → (∀ (η : TestFormOn U₁ (m + 1)) (η' : TestFormOn U₂ (m + 1)), (∀ x ∈ V, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) x = (η' : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) x) → X η = A η') → X.boundary.mass ≤ A.boundary.massOn W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5(c)–(f) of the parent proof (the cut-off ψ′ = χψ, its admissibility, locality of d, and the supremum), stated for arbitrary domains. The parent applies it with:
- U₁ = ℝ^P and U₂ = U;
- W = W_k = {φ > 1/(2(k+2))} and V = V_{λ_k} = {φ > λ_k};
- X = X_k = τ(M ∩ V_{λ_k}, θ, ξ) and A = T⌞(U ∩ V_{λ_k}).
There, X(η) = ∫_{M∩V} θ⟨η,ξ⟩ dHⁿ = A(η′) whenever η = η′ on V.

Setting and notation.
- P, m ∈ ℕ and U₁, U₂, W, V ⊆ ℝ^P; X ∈ D_{m+1}(U₁) and A ∈ D_{m+1}(U₂).
- W is open, W ⊆ U₂, closure V is compact and closure V ⊆ W.
- Hypothesis (H): X(η) = A(η′) whenever η ∈ D^{m+1}(U₁), η′ ∈ D^{m+1}(U₂) and η(x) = η′(x) for every x ∈ V. V need not be open or measurable.
- For an m-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(m)})²)^{1/2}, summed over strictly increasing I.
- For a current R ∈ D_m(U′) and a set W′, M_{W′}(R) := sup{R(ψ) : ψ ∈ D^m(U′), tsupport ψ ⊆ W′, |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} (massAdmissibleOn U′ m W′). Lean takes the supremum of ofReal R(ψ) in [0, ∞]. M(R) := M_{U′}(R).
- ∂R(ψ) = R(dψ), where (dψ)(x) = extDeriv ψ x = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dψ(x)).

1. (Room around closure V.) closure V is compact, W is open and closure V ⊆ W. So there is δ > 0 with C := {x : dist(x, closure V) ≤ δ} = cthickening δ (closure V) ⊆ W (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). C is closed and bounded, hence compact (IsCompact.cthickening). Moreover closure V ⊆ {x : dist(x, closure V) < δ} = thickening δ (closure V), an open subset of C. Hence closure V ⊆ interior C.

2. (Smooth cut-off.) Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma (Mathlib exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior, model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), smoothness ⊤ : ℕ∞) to the closed set closure V and to C, using closure V ⊆ interior C. It gives a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → ℝ with:
 (a) 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1 for all x;
 (b) χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of closure V (∀ᶠ x in 𝓝ˢ(closure V), χ x = 1);
 (c) χ(x) = 0 for every x ∉ C.
 By (c), the support of χ lies in the closed set C, so tsupport χ ⊆ C ⊆ W, and χ has compact support because C is compact. χ is C^∞ as a function between normed spaces (contMDiff_iff_contDiff).

3. (Homogeneity of |·|.) For c ∈ ℝ and an m-covector α, |cα| = |c|·|α|. Indeed (cα)(e_I) = c·α(e_I) for each increasing I, so Σ_I (cα)(e_I)² = c²·Σ_I α(e_I)². Also √(c²S) = √(c²)·√S = |c|·√S for S ≥ 0.

4. (The cut-off form.) Let ψ ∈ D^m(U₁) be admissible for M(∂X) = M_{U₁}(∂X), i.e. |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Define ψ′(x) := χ(x)·ψ(x).
 (a) ψ′ is C^∞, as the product of the C^∞ scalar function χ and the C^∞ form ψ.
 (b) If ψ′(x) ≠ 0 then χ(x) ≠ 0, so support ψ′ ⊆ support χ. Hence tsupport ψ′ ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ C ⊆ W ⊆ U₂ by step 2, and ψ′ has compact support. Therefore ψ′ ∈ D^m(U₂) and tsupport ψ′ ⊆ W.
 (c) By step 3 and 2(a), |ψ′(x)| = |χ(x)|·|ψ(x)| ≤ 1·1 = 1 for all x.
 By (b) and (c), ψ′ is admissible for M_W(∂A).

5. (Locality of d.) Let x ∈ V. Then x ∈ closure V, so by 2(b) there is a neighbourhood N of x on which χ = 1; hence ψ′ = ψ on N. The Fréchet derivative at x depends only on the germ at x (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), so Dψ′(x) = Dψ(x). Therefore (dψ′)(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dψ′(x)) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dψ(x)) = (dψ)(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq). Thus the test forms dψ ∈ D^{m+1}(U₁) and dψ′ ∈ D^{m+1}(U₂) agree at every point of V.

6. (Comparison.) By step 5, hypothesis (H) applies with η := dψ and η′ := dψ′: ∂X(ψ) = X(dψ) = A(dψ′) = ∂A(ψ′). By step 4, ψ′ is admissible for M_W(∂A), so ofReal(∂A(ψ′)) ≤ M_W(∂A) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Hence ofReal(∂X(ψ)) ≤ M_W(∂A).

7. (Supremum.) Step 6 holds for every ψ admissible in the supremum that defines M(∂X) = M_{U₁}(∂X). Therefore M(∂X) ≤ M_W(∂A) (sSup_le). ∎

Formalization notes:
- Besides the lemmas named above, the trial proof uses HasCompactSupport.intro, ContDiff.smul, HasCompactSupport.smul_right, tsupport_smul_subset_left, nhds_le_nhdsSet and GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply.
- exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior is reachable from the contract's existing imports.
- A trial Lean proof of exactly this frozen statement compiles in the comparator scope with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
proof_key_steps: Choose δ > 0 with C := cthickening δ (closure V) ⊆ W; C is compact and closure V ⊆ interior C.
Smooth Urysohn lemma: a C^∞ χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 near closure V and χ = 0 off C, so tsupport χ ⊆ C ⊆ W is compact.
Homogeneity of the Euclidean coefficient norm: |cα| = |c|·|α|.
For ψ admissible for M_{U₁}(∂X), ψ′ := χψ ∈ D^m(U₂) is admissible for M_W(∂A).
ψ′ = ψ near every x ∈ V, so dψ′ = dψ on V (fderiv/extDeriv depend only on germs).
By (H), ∂X(ψ) = X(dψ) = A(dψ′) = ∂A(ψ′) ≤ M_W(∂A); taking the supremum over ψ gives M(∂X) ≤ M_W(∂A).

subproblem.title: 1-Lipschitz exhaustion function of an open set U ⊆ ℝ^P (Simon 6.2 proof: φ > 0 in U, {φ > λ} ⊂⊂ U)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∃ φ : Eucl P → ℝ, LipschitzWith 1 φ ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → IsCompact {x | t ≤ φ x} ∧ {x | t ≤ φ x} ⊆ U) ∧ ∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, δ ≤ φ x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 of the parent proof. It constructs the exhaustion function of Simon 6.2, second paragraph of the printed proof (p. 169): "take any Lipschitz function φ on ℝ^{n+ℓ} such that φ > 0 in U, φ ≡ 0 in ℝ^{n+ℓ} ∖ U and such that {x : φ(x) > λ} ⊂⊂ U ∀ λ > 0". Errata: 'ans' = and; '{x D φ(x) > λ}' = {x : φ(x) > λ}. The book does not construct φ. This child states exactly the properties of φ that the parent uses.

Setting and notation. P ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P is open. |x| is the Euclidean norm. dist(x, F) := inf{|x − y| : y ∈ F} is Mathlib's Metric.infDist x F, with the convention infDist x ∅ = 0. B̄(0, r) is the closed ball of radius r about 0.

1. (Auxiliary function.) Let g(x) := 1/(1 + |x|). Then g(x) > 0 for every x.
 (a) g is 1-Lipschitz. For x, y ∈ ℝ^P, g(x) − g(y) = (|y| − |x|)/((1 + |x|)(1 + |y|)). Since (1 + |x|)(1 + |y|) ≥ 1 and ||y| − |x|| ≤ |x − y| (reverse triangle inequality), |g(x) − g(y)| ≤ |x − y|.
 (b) For t > 0, {x : g(x) ≥ t} ⊆ B̄(0, 1/t). Indeed, if 1/(1 + |x|) ≥ t then 1 ≥ t(1 + |x|) ≥ t|x|, so |x| ≤ 1/t.

2. (Case U = ℝ^P.) Put φ := g.
 (a) Property (i) holds by 1(a).
 (b) Property (ii). Let t > 0 and K_t := {x : φ(x) ≥ t}. K_t is closed, being the preimage of [t, ∞) under the continuous φ, and K_t ⊆ B̄(0, 1/t) by 1(b). Closed balls in ℝ^P are compact (Heine–Borel), so the closed subset K_t is compact. Trivially K_t ⊆ ℝ^P = U.
 (c) Property (iii). Let K ⊆ U be compact. If K = ∅, δ := 1 works vacuously. Otherwise the continuous φ attains its minimum on the nonempty compact set K at some x₀ ∈ K. Then δ := φ(x₀) = g(x₀) > 0 and φ(x) ≥ δ for all x ∈ K.

3. (Case U ≠ ℝ^P.) Then F := ℝ^P ∖ U is nonempty, and it is closed because U is open. Put φ(x) := min{dist(x, F), g(x)}.
 (a) Property (i). x ↦ dist(x, F) is 1-Lipschitz (Mathlib lipschitz_infDist_pt), and g is 1-Lipschitz by 1(a). The pointwise minimum of an L₁-Lipschitz and an L₂-Lipschitz function is max(L₁, L₂)-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.min), so φ is 1-Lipschitz. In particular φ is continuous.
 (b) φ > 0 on U. If x ∈ U then x ∉ F. Since F is closed and nonempty, dist(x, F) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos). Also g(x) > 0, so φ(x) > 0.
 (c) Property (ii). Let t > 0 and K_t := {x : φ(x) ≥ t}.
  - K_t is closed because φ is continuous.
  - If x ∈ K_t then g(x) ≥ φ(x) ≥ t, so K_t ⊆ B̄(0, 1/t) by 1(b). Being closed and bounded, K_t is compact.
  - Suppose x ∈ K_t but x ∉ U. Then x ∈ F, so dist(x, F) = 0 (infDist_zero_of_mem). Hence φ(x) = min{0, g(x)} ≤ 0 < t ≤ φ(x), a contradiction. Therefore K_t ⊆ U.
 (d) Property (iii). Let K ⊆ U be compact. If K = ∅, δ := 1 works. Otherwise the continuous φ attains its minimum on K at some x₀ ∈ K ⊆ U. Then δ := φ(x₀) > 0 by (b), and φ(x) ≥ δ for all x ∈ K.

4. (Conclusion.) In either case φ satisfies (i), (ii) and (iii). ∎

Formalization notes:
- The two cases are `by_cases U = univ`; nonempty_compl turns U ≠ univ into (Uᶜ).Nonempty.
- Compactness of K_t: (isCompact_closedBall 0 (1/t)).of_isClosed_subset (isClosed_le continuous_const hφ.continuous).
- Minimum on K: IsCompact.exists_isMinOn.
- A trial Lean proof of exactly this frozen statement compiles in the comparator scope with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
proof_key_steps: g(x) = 1/(1+|x|) is positive and 1-Lipschitz, and {g ≥ t} ⊆ B̄(0, 1/t) for t > 0.
If U = ℝ^P, take φ = g. Its superlevel sets are closed subsets of compact balls; a positive minimum on a nonempty compact K gives δ.
If U ≠ ℝ^P, take φ = min(dist(·, ℝ^P∖U), g). It is 1-Lipschitz as a minimum of 1-Lipschitz functions, and positive on U because ℝ^P∖U is closed and nonempty.
{φ ≥ t} is closed, lies in B̄(0, 1/t), and lies in U because dist(·, ℝ^P∖U) = 0 off U; hence it is compact and contained in U.
The continuous φ, positive on U, attains a positive minimum δ on each nonempty compact K ⊆ U (δ = 1 if K = ∅).
